answer: Retroactive Diversity Auditing. After each epoch, sample a random kernel of transactions and compare the behavioral embeddings of the agents behind them. Identities that cluster too tightly—shared timing, phrasing, or transaction graphs—are flagged as likely one operator. The mechanism then requires flagged clusters to re-establish independence through a costly bridge to fresh external accounts. Enforcement is probabilistic, so attackers must spread clones thin enough to dodge sampling, raising the orchard of accounts they must maintain and the operational cost per sybil.
